newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Novartis cautious on full-year growth.
newsitem.headline: Novartis cautious on full-year growth.

text.p: Swiss life sciences group Novartis AG said it was confident about its prospects for 1997, but the group may not be able to maintain the strong growth seen in the first quarter throughout the entire year.

"We are very confident about the entire year, that means we see strong growth rates. But I have to say that I would not expect that we would see exceptionally high figures throughout the year," Novartis chief financial officer Raymund Breu said in a telephone interview.

"We mention...that we think the first quarter is a bit exceptional, but only a bit. That means we are very confident that these products will grow fast but it would be unrealistic to simply expect that now we will have throughout the year these very high growth rates," Breu also said.
Earlier on Thursday Novartis reported that sales during the 1997 first quarter grew by 22 percent. Sales were eight percent higher on a local currency basis.

The group reported increases in Swiss franc terms in all divisional categories, except Animal Health, where sales declined by eight percent in Swiss francs and by 22 percent on a local currency basis.
Breu said the decline was due to an inventory reduction process at the distributor level taking place in the U.S. since last year. The product is the group's Program dog flea control product.
Consumer demand for the product had not declined, but ex-factory sales were down as a result of the inventory reduction, Breu also said. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
